practiceReport.name: D.J. Reed
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (9th NFL season, 94% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Reed expressed pessimism Wednesday that he would be cleared to return for Week 11 due to a hip injury, and the veteran defensive back will, in fact, be sidelined for a third consecutive game. Khalil Dorsey will likely start opposite Rock Ya-Sin at outside cornerback in the absence of Reed, whose next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bears on Thanksgiving Day.

practiceReport.beatComment: A shoulder injury limited Rakestraw's practice reps during Week 11 prep. Reed (hip) also sidelined, Khalil Dorsey figures to start opposite Rock Ya-Sin at outside cornerback. Rakestraw's next opportunity to play is Thanksgiving Day against the Bears.

practiceReport.name: Kerby Joseph
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
practiceReport.beatComment: Joseph was a full participant in his return to the active roster Wednesday. The free safety is set to make his 2026 debut in Week 11 against the Buccaneers, finally reuniting with strong safety Brian Branch after both spent lengthy periods on the Lions' reserve lists.

practiceReport.name: Khalil Dorsey
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (CB) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Dorsey hurt his wrist early in Sunday's game and was initially deemed questionable to return. The veteran cornerback has since been able to re-enter the game, albeit with a club over the hand that he injured. Dorsey has been working in a rotational role at cornerback, logging a defensive snap share between 32 and 38 percent three straight weeks.

practiceReport.name: Sione Vaki
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (RB) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Vaki has been tending to an ankle issue for three weeks running, but he's still suited up on the previous two occasions, combining for nine carries for 42 yards (4.7 YPC) and three catches (on three targets) for 19 yards. With active status confirmed for Week 11, he'll continue to serve as a complement to No. 1 RB Jahmyr Gibbs.

practiceReport.name: Tyler Lacy
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (DT) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Lacy was limited in practice all week due to a shoulder injury, but he's been cleared to play in Sunday's home game. He's expected to take on an elevated role at defensive end in the absence of Aidan Hutchinson, who is out for the rest of the season due to a torn ACL. Lacy has accumulated 12 tackles (four solo) through nine regular-season games.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Cade Mays
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Mays missed the Lions' two prior games due to an ankle injury that he sustained against the Vikings in Week 8. His placement on IR means he's required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against Minnesota. Juice Scruggs figures to be the Lions' starting center for as long as Mays is sidelined.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Aidan Hutchinson
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Hutchinson's move to IR was merely a formality after he was diagnosed with a torn ACL in his right knee following his early exit from this past Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft has now succumbed to two season-ending injuries through his first five years in the league, after a fractured tibia and fibula in his left leg cut short his 2024 campaign.
